text:
maya: Noticing elevated error rates from eu-west GPU pool since ~09:05 UTC. p95 latency spikes + token failures. Logs show repeated 'fabric: kv cache miss' and 'grpc: transport: connection error'.
jon: Looking at node metrics now. Some hosts show high rx/tx errors on IB interface. Could be fabric routing.
liam: Confirmed intermittent BGP flap between eu-west1-rackB and spine-3 causing packet reorder. We're seeing drops on rtr-12 -> rtr-9.
maya: Symptoms: customers on eu-west get 502s for streaming, model fallbacks triggering to smaller variants, and dedicated pools unaffected for some tenants.
oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-20260318-2138765432 - eu-west GPU fabric degradation. Severity: high. Bridge: #incident-2138765432.
jon: Quick triage: set autoscale to 0.8 min for eu-west GPU pool to reduce scheduling pressure and lower retry storms. Applying now.
opsbot: Command run by jon: `rbctl cluster update --region eu-west --pool gpu --min-scale 0.8` -> OK.
liam: Routing teams are pushing a temporary next-hop change to avoid rtr-9. Applying BGP community to steer around faulty fabric path. ETA 12m.
eva: Noted KV cache hits drop ~40% when traffic crosses affected racks. That explains repeated KV warmups and token cost spike.
sara: Support: drafting status page. Proposal: "Partial degradation in eu-west impacting streaming responses and higher latency. We're routing around affected fabric and shifting some traffic to eu-central; next update in 20 minutes." Thoughts?
maya: Good. Add note about potential transient model fallbacks and higher per-token cost while we route/replicate. Customers on Dedicated unaffected.
sara: OK adding: "Dedicated customers on reserved capacity are not affected; Hosted users might see occasional fallbacks and slight cost increase while we mitigate."
jon: We should start gradual traffic shift to eu-central for non-data-residency customers. Plan: 30% -> 60% over 15m, monitor error budget. Does routing policy allow that without causing overload?
liam: eu-central has ~18% spare headroom. Can accept up to 40% of current eu-west baseline. We'll cap shift at 35% to be safe.
maya: Initiating shift: `trafficctl reroute --from eu-west --to eu-central --percent 30 --policy gradual`
opsbot: Command run by maya: `trafficctl reroute ...` -> accepted. Starting step 1/3.
sara: Status page published (draft): "We are investigating increased errors and latency in eu-west GPU pool caused by a network fabric issue. We are routing traffic to alternate region to reduce user impact. ETA for next update: 20 minutes."
support-team: Flagging top customers in eu-west for proactive outreach. Sending queued DM templates now.
eva: Monitoring: kv-cache hitrate recovering on nodes once traffic routes change. Error rate down ~28% so far.
liam: BGP change holding, fabric team still validating. We might need to cordon one rack if we see persistent packet corruption.
jon: If cordoning becomes necessary, we'll need to pre-warm KV caches in eu-central to avoid regen storm. Schedule warmup job: `warmup-promptset --region eu-central --target 5k-keys`
maya: Launched warmup job.
opsbot: Job queued: warmup-promptset (eu-central) started by maya.
sara: I'll update status page: include note about warmup and potential transient cost impact.
support-team: One customer (Acme Widgets) escalated to Priority 1. Assigned to @eva for liaison.
eva: On it. Provided ETA: we'll route their traffic to eu-central and confirm continuity within 10m.
jon: Tentative rollback plan if eu-central nears capacity: throttle non-critical streaming and enable model quantization fallbacks to reduce tokens.
maya: Agree. We'll aim to keep customer-facing uninterrupted, cost tradeoffs acceptable short term.
liam: Continue watching RX/TX errors. If corruption persists after 30m, we schedule rack eviction and full hardware replacement window.
oncall-bot: Update: Incident INC-20260318-2138765432 severity remains high. Next update at 2138766030 UTC or sooner.
sara: Posted status page: https://status.redwood.ai/incident/INC-20260318-2138765432 - message mirrors draft.
maya: Current metrics: errors down 45%, p95 latency down 22%. Still seeing intermittent resets but stability improving.
support-team: Outreach batch 2 sent.
eva: Acme confirmed service continuity after reroute. No data loss observed.
liam: Will keep fabric filters applied for 2h, then attempt gradual re-introduction of rtr-9 path.
jon: After 1h baseline OK, we'll revert traffic and scale back autoscale change.
sara: Final status note pending: include timeline, root-cause (fabric forwarding plane corruption on rtr-9), mitigations, and customer impact summary.
maya: Thanks all. Stand down unless new regressions.
